name: Glean
subcategory: enterprise work search and AI assistant
tagline: Permission-aware AI search and chat across every app a company uses.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Glean sells annual enterprise contracts with per-seat pricing plus platform fees, quoted by sales.

verdictSummary: The demo looks like a chat box over your documents, which is why people think it is a weekend project. The actual product is a hundred-plus connectors that continuously crawl Slack, Jira, Confluence, Salesforce, Drive, Github and the rest, and then mirror every source system's access control list so a search never leaks a doc the asker is not allowed to read. That permission mirroring is the whole thing, and it is boring, endless, per-connector maintenance work with legal consequences when it breaks. A local RAG index over the files on your own laptop is genuinely useful and very buildable, but it is a different product: one user, one permission set, no company. If you are one person, you do not need Glean, and if you are a company, you cannot build it in a sitting.
coreLoopDIY: Indexes a folder of your own local files and exported chat or doc dumps, embeds the chunks, and answers questions over them with citations back to the source file.
requirements: An API key for an embedding and chat model, or a local model via Ollama
Local copies or exports of the content you want searchable
Comfort re-running the indexer manually or on a cron
whatYouLose: Live connectors to Slack, Jira, Confluence, Salesforce, Drive and the other few dozen systems where work actually lives
Permission-aware results: your local index has no concept of who is allowed to see what
Continuous incremental crawling, so your index is as fresh as the last time you remembered to run it
People search, org context and the knowledge-graph ranking that makes Glean answers feel company-aware instead of document-aware
SOC 2 and enterprise audit trails, which is the reason security teams sign off on this category at all
moatNotes: Every connector is a permanent maintenance contract with someone else's API and someone else's permission model. The count is the moat, and the count only goes up.
whyPeopleStillPay: Companies do not buy Glean because chat over documents is hard. They buy it because nobody internally wants to own sixty OAuth integrations, per-source access control syncing, and the incident review that happens the first time search surfaces a compensation spreadsheet to the wrong person. The value is that a vendor takes that liability, keeps the crawlers running, and passes the security questionnaire. An individual gets almost none of that value and can happily self-host a local index instead.
notes: A citation-backed RAG box over your own files is a weekend build and worth doing. The moat is not the retrieval, it is a hundred live connectors that faithfully mirror every source system's permissions, forever.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user semantic search and Q&A tool over my own files. Call it "shelf".

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, plain server-rendered Jinja2 templates plus a little vanilla JS. No React, no build step.
- SQLite for everything: documents, chunks, and vectors stored as blobs, plus an FTS5 table for keyword search.
- Embeddings and chat via the OpenAI API, model names in .env so they are swappable. Also support a LOCAL_MODE=ollama switch that hits a local Ollama endpoint instead.

In scope:
- A CLI command `shelf index /path/to/folder` that walks the folder recursively and ingests .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, .html, .csv. Use pypdf and python-docx. Skip anything over 20MB.
- Chunk to roughly 800 tokens with 100 token overlap, keep the source path, page or heading, and modified time on every chunk.
- Store a content hash per file so re-running the indexer only re-embeds files that actually changed. Deletions remove their chunks.
- Hybrid retrieval: FTS5 keyword search plus cosine similarity over embeddings, merged with reciprocal rank fusion, top 12 chunks.
- A single page at / with a search box. Show ranked results with the matching snippet and a clickable local file path.
- An "Ask" mode that stuffs the top chunks into a prompt and streams an answer with inline numbered citations that map to the source files. If retrieval is weak, say so instead of guessing.
- `shelf watch /path` using watchdog for incremental reindexing while it runs.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, permissions, multi-tenancy, any third-party SaaS connectors, OAuth, telemetry, Docker, deployment configs.

Rules:
- All secrets in .env, read via python-dotenv, and ship a .env.example. Never commit keys.
- Everything runs on localhost and binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
- One `uv` or `requirements.txt` install, then `uvicorn` to run. Put the exact two commands at the top of the README.
- Include a `shelf stats` command printing file count, chunk count, and index size on disk.
- Write it so an empty database bootstraps itself on first run with no migration tooling.
